items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.

September 30 is a day to witness and honour the healing journey of residential school survivors and their families. It is a day to pause and recognize the lasting impacts that residential schools have had on thousands of Indigenous families and communities who continue to work through various stages of grieving and healing.
We encourage all residents of Waterloo and the Region to stop, reflect, learn and act.

Attend a memorial event organized by local Indigenous leaders. Explore learning resources curated by our local libraries. Donate to Indigenous-led organizations. These small but important signs of solidarity are important today and all year round.
As a City, we re-commit ourselves to the long-term work of reconciliation so we have a better community for the seven generations yet to come.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: City of Waterloo Official Plan Review
notes: (Phase 1), OPA No. 58
Prepared by: Ric Martins
Ward No.: City-Wide
Ric Martins gave a presentation outlining phase one of the Official Plan Review, as well as the timeline for future phases. He responded to questions of Council.

Addison Milne-Price, Planner, Design Plan Services Inc. provided comments regarding Commercial and Mixed-Use Land Uses, and offered recommendations on specific lands. Joel Cotter and Ric Martins responded to questions of Council.

Sam Goncalves-Horton, VP Activism, Planning Students Association, UW NDP Club, Violeta Manastirliu, Planning Students Association and Manuela D'Cunha, Planning Students Association gave a presentation about the need for a reduction in parking minimums, and changes to the parking policies. They then responded to questions of Council. Ric Martins also responded to questions of Council.

Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo offered her comments on the Official Plan Review, from Greenhouse Gas emissions from traffic and possible contradictions in the goals for the Uptown Primary Node. She then responded to questions of Council. Ric Martins also responded to questions of Council.
Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke in support of the UW Planning Students Association in their request to remove parking minimums, and about the need for more Affordable Housing.
Phil Marfisi, Resident of Waterloo also spoke in support of the reduction of parking minimums, as well as the need for more flexibility in commercial use buildings in the suburbs.

As no one else was present to speak to the Official Plan Review, the Chair concluded the Statutory Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Bodaly wanted to highlight that the Clair Hills Community Association hosted a fun fair yesterday, September 22, at St. Moritz Park. There were staff there talking about the revitalization of the park. He noted that this could be the last event for the Association as they’re struggling to replace members of the Board and volunteerism is down. He added that Neighbourhood Associations are important to communities and bring vibrancy to the areas, and it’s important to support them.

Councillor Wright had a weekend was full of activities, including connecting with the Spinning Wheels team, a volunteer-run organization that raises money for Parkinson’s supports in the community. She learned a lot about how addressing Parkinson’s can “raise the tide” for all people experiencing neurological impacts. She also noted that Canada has the highest rate of Parkinson’s per capita.

Councillor Wright also spoke about how Shalom Counselling held their mental health walk, 10,000 Steps for Mental Health on Saturday, September 21. They surpassed their fundraising goal and had fantastic volunteers. They offer a sliding scale of rates for their counselling services. The Kidney Foundation also had their Kidney Walk on Sunday, September 22, and they also surpassed their fundraising goal and it was great to honour Dr. Tom Liu, who had been a pillar of renal care at Grand River Hospital.
Councillor Wright also mentioned that Emmanuel at Brighton is celebrating their 60th anniversary. They provide childcare support for working families.

Councillor Roe mentioned the 3rd Annual Canadian Arab Women’s Association Festival in Kitchener on Saturday, September 21. It was a fantastic event with music, food and a market. The Association is being recognized by the United Nations for the work they do empowering women and building community.
Councillor Roe also gave a shout-out to Lumen on Saturday, September 21, and the staff and volunteers who helped put it on. The crowds were huge and the installations were amazing.

Councillor Vasic wanted to highlight two events that she couldn’t go to, as the weekend was so busy. There was a neighbourhood street party in her neighbourhood, and she offered her thanks to the Neighbourhoods team for the funding, so that they’re able to run these events each year. She also mentioned the counter-protest in Kitchener on Friday, September 20, offering support for 2SLGBTQIA+ folks, and making sure children and youth have access to resources, people, and the education they need to feel like they can be their full selves.

Councillor Vasic also mentioned the Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery is holding their flagship fundraising event, instead of a gala. They’re running a “whodunnit” event, where you have to try to capture “The Paris Prowler.” It is happening on Saturday, October 26 and tickets are limited.
Mayor McCabe mentioned that the weekend was very full and offered thanks to those in the community, especially the volunteers and staff for all of their hard work in putting these events together.
